blocks.text: FY2025 was the year faster growth turned into operating leverage. Revenue was {fact:revenue-fy2025} in FY2025, up {fact:revenue-growth-fy2025} from {fact:revenue-fy2024} in FY2024 [src-18]. Income from operations was {fact:op-income-fy2025} in FY2025, up {fact:op-income-growth-fy2025} from {fact:op-income-fy2024} in FY2024, while net income was {fact:net-income-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-27] [src-28]. Operating margin was {fact:op-margin-fy2025} in FY2025, compared with {fact:op-margin-fy2024} in FY2024, because operating expenses grew more slowly than revenue rather than declined [src-27].

Cash generation ran ahead of earnings. Operating cash flow was {fact:ocf-fy2025} in FY2025, above net income of {fact:net-income-fy2025} in the same year, supported by noncash adjustments led by stock-based compensation of {fact:sbc-fy2025} in FY2025, partly offset by receivables growth net of higher contract liabilities [src-31] [src-28] [src-33]. After deducting cash paid for property and equipment of {fact:capex-fy2025} in FY2025, the remaining operating cash was {fact:cash-remainder-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-31] [src-32]. That remainder is analyst-defined and excludes marketable-securities, financing and other investing uses, so it does not establish distributable cash.

Capacity stayed cash-rich, while future demands remain separate from cash already paid. Cash plus marketable securities were {fact:liquidity-dec2025} at December 31, 2025, against {fact:current-liab-dec2025} of current liabilities at the same date, with no outstanding balances under the {fact:revolver-capacity-dec2025} revolving facility [src-68] [src-69] [src-70] [src-79]. One amended cloud-services agreement carries a lifetime floor of at least {fact:cloud-commit-fy2025} over ten contract years through September 30, 2033, not a remaining balance at year-end, with {fact:cloud-satisfied-fy2025} satisfied of {fact:cloud-current-year-fy2025} for the contract year beginning October 1, 2025 and ending September 30, 2026 [src-57] [src-61]. The separate aggregate of remaining enforceable purchase commitments is detailed by payment period in **Investment and commitments**, and only enforceable and legally binding contracts are included [src-62]. Paid cash, carrying amounts, noncash additions and these future commitments use different bases and dates and must not be added together.

Higher earnings drove per-share growth even as the share count rose: diluted earnings per share were {fact:eps-diluted-fy2025} in FY2025 on diluted shares of {fact:shares-diluted-fy2025} in FY2025, and shares outstanding rose {fact:shares-out-growth-fy2025} to {fact:shares-out-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-35] [src-37] [src-74]. Stock-based compensation of {fact:sbc-fy2025} in FY2025 and a full valuation allowance of {fact:valuation-allow-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 keep comparability conditional on dilution and any future allowance release [src-33] [src-38]. Remaining performance obligations of {fact:rpo-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 cover only noncancelable contracted revenue, so broader deal value that presumes options and no termination is not assured revenue [src-09] [src-15] [src-10].

sections.title: Key findings

blocks.text: Palantir sells access to four software platforms — **Gotham, Foundry, Apollo and AIP** — that integrate customer data and operations so software can run in almost any environment [src-01]. Gotham and Foundry each serve as a central operating system for customers, while AIP provides an integrated architecture to both that can bring AI to decisions, with Ontology at the heart and Apollo backing deployment [src-02].

Revenue comes from subscriptions to access the platforms plus services. The filing groups the offer as Palantir Cloud hosted access with ongoing O&M — operations and maintenance [src-82] — services, On-Premises term licenses with ongoing O&M services, and professional services [src-05]. Cloud subscriptions grant continuous hosted access and are generally recognized over the contract term on a ratable basis [src-06], and On-Premises license plus O&M is treated as a single obligation likewise recognized over the term [src-13]. Professional work — support, configuration, training and ontology and data-modeling support — is on demand through the service period.

Customers are government and commercial institutions worldwide. Palantir reported {fact:revenue-fy2025} of revenue in FY2025 and had 954 customers during the period ended December 31, 2025, compared with 711 customers during the period ended December 31, 2024 [src-81]. A customer is an organization from which revenue was recognized during the trailing twelve-month period [src-04]. Government revenue was {fact:gov-revenue-fy2025} and commercial revenue was {fact:com-revenue-fy2025} in FY2025, with government modestly larger than commercial. U.S. revenue was {fact:us-revenue-fy2025} in FY2025. No AIP-only revenue split is disclosed, so the filing does not establish how much of the total is AI-specific.

blocks.text: Palantir accelerated in FY2025. Revenue was {fact:revenue-fy2025} in FY2025, up {fact:revenue-growth-fy2025} from {fact:revenue-fy2024} in FY2024, after {fact:revenue-growth-fy2024} growth from FY2023 to FY2024 [src-18]. Income from operations, net income and operating cash flow all moved in the same direction across FY2023 to FY2025, with operating income growing {fact:op-income-growth-fy2025} and net income growing {fact:net-income-growth-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-27] [src-28]. The scale of profit growth relative to revenue growth points to operating leverage rather than a single non-operating gain.

Operating cash flow was {fact:ocf-fy2025} in FY2025, above net income of {fact:net-income-fy2025} in the same year, and grew {fact:ocf-growth-fy2025} from {fact:ocf-fy2024} in FY2024 [src-31] [src-28]. Cash paid for property and equipment was {fact:capex-fy2025} in FY2025, up from {fact:capex-fy2024} in FY2024 but small alongside cash generation [src-32]. Earnings and cash therefore tell a consistent direction story in FY2025; the reconciliation between them and what cash remains after investment belong to the cash-flow analysis, not to this scorecard.

Gross margin was {fact:gross-margin-fy2025} in FY2025 compared with {fact:gross-margin-fy2024} in FY2024, while operating margin was {fact:op-margin-fy2025} in FY2025 compared with {fact:op-margin-fy2024} in FY2024 [src-26] [src-27]. Total operating expenses were {fact:opex-fy2025} in FY2025 versus {fact:opex-fy2024} in FY2024, growing more slowly than revenue and lifting operating margin by much more than gross margin [src-39] [src-40] [src-41]. That pattern is operating leverage from slower expense growth, not a cut in absolute spending.

Cost of revenue was {fact:cost-revenue-fy2025} in FY2025 versus {fact:cost-revenue-fy2024} in FY2024 [src-25]. Management attributes the increase to third-party cloud hosting, subcontractors, field-service representatives and payroll costs [src-42]. Sales and marketing was {fact:sales-marketing-fy2025} in FY2025, research and development was {fact:rd-fy2025} in FY2025 and general and administrative was {fact:ga-fy2025} in FY2025, each higher in dollars than in FY2024 but lower as a share of a faster-growing revenue base [src-39] [src-40] [src-41]. Net margin was {fact:net-margin-fy2025} in FY2025, above operating margin, reflecting pre-tax income of {fact:pretax-fy2025} in FY2025 and a provision of {fact:tax-provision-fy2025} in FY2025 with an effective rate of {fact:effective-tax-rate-fy2025} [src-28] [src-29] [src-30].

Palantir reports two operating segments — Government, serving U.S. and non-U.S. agencies, and Commercial, serving non-government industries. Segment profitability is evaluated on contribution, defined as segment revenue less related cost of revenue and sales and marketing expenses, excluding stock-based compensation [src-07]. Costs not directly attributable are allocated pro rata by headcount and time on the account, with direct costs such as cloud hosting allocated directly [src-14]. Contribution therefore excludes research and development, general and administrative, and stock-based compensation, and is reconciled to consolidated income from operations. It is not a standalone-company margin.

blocks.text: Stock-based compensation was {fact:sbc-fy2025} in FY2025 compared with {fact:sbc-fy2024} in FY2024 and {fact:sbc-fy2023} in FY2023 [src-33]. The filing reports a small year-over-year decrease in FY2025 [src-43]. The charge is allocated across cost of revenue and operating expenses and is excluded from segment contribution [src-07]. It is added back in operating cash flow because it is noncash, but shareholders still bear its economic cost through dilution or cash used to offset dilution.

The provision for income taxes was {fact:tax-provision-fy2025} in FY2025 on pre-tax income of {fact:pretax-fy2025} in FY2025, an effective rate of {fact:effective-tax-rate-fy2025} [src-29] [src-30]. The filing says the year-over-year increase in the provision was not material [src-44]. The company continued to maintain a full valuation allowance against relevant deferred tax assets [src-45], with the allowance at {fact:valuation-allow-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 versus {fact:valuation-allow-dec2024} at December 31, 2024 [src-38]. Period comparability therefore remains affected by when, if ever, that allowance is released.

Basic earnings per share were {fact:eps-basic-fy2025} in FY2025 and diluted earnings per share were {fact:eps-diluted-fy2025} in FY2025, up from {fact:eps-diluted-fy2024} in FY2024 [src-34] [src-35]. Basic weighted-average shares were {fact:shares-basic-fy2025} in FY2025 and diluted shares were {fact:shares-diluted-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-36] [src-37]. EPS growth in FY2025 came chiefly from higher earnings spread over a larger share count, so the per-share result should be read as profit growth less dilution, not as a reduced share count.

Operating cash flow exceeded net income in FY2025: net income was {fact:net-income-fy2025} and operating cash flow was {fact:ocf-fy2025} [src-28] [src-31]. The statement bridge ties exactly from income through adjustments and working-capital changes to operating cash. Noncash adjustments totaled {fact:noncash-group-fy2025} in FY2025, dominated by stock-based compensation of {fact:sbc-fy2025} [src-33]. Working-capital changes were a net use of {fact:wc-group-fy2025} in FY2025, as the presented accounts-receivable use of {fact:ar-change-pres-fy2025} exceeded the contract-liabilities source of {fact:contract-liab-change-fy2025} [src-50] [src-53]. Accrual earnings and cash differ but are bridged; they are not interchangeable.

Cash paid for property and equipment was {fact:capex-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-32]. That outflow differs in basis and date from carrying amounts, noncash additions and future commitments. Property and equipment net was {fact:ppe-net-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-55], a depreciated stock rather than cash paid in the year. Right-of-use additions of {fact:rou-additions-fy2025} in FY2025 were noncash and are excluded from cash paid [src-56].

The cloud figures below are different measures on different horizons, not FY2025 cash paid. Satisfied is the filing's term and does not by itself establish cash paid.

Separately, aggregate remaining enforceable noncancelable purchase commitments as of December 31, 2025 are shown in the table below in thousands. blocks.text:
Operating lease expense was {fact:lease-expense-fy2025} in FY2025, while cash paid for operating lease liabilities was {fact:lease-cash-paid-fy2025} in FY2025 as supplemental disclosure [src-58] [src-59]. The filing does not state where that cash is classified in the cash flow statement, so this report does not claim the filing places it in operating cash flow; {quote:src-65} so no material lease principal and interest split is established.

Noncash additions of {fact:rou-additions-fy2025} in FY2025 create matched assets and liabilities without cash at commencement [src-56]. Recognized total lease liabilities were {fact:lease-liab-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-60].

The annual calendar above from Note 7 shows undiscounted commitments, sublease income and net commitments for 2026 through 2030, thereafter and totals, in thousands as of December 31, 2025. Its gross undiscounted total less sublease income equals the net undiscounted amount, with imputed interest shown on a separate row to reach the final row labeled Total operating lease liabilities in the Net Lease Commitments column; the filing does not label that net column as present value and does not state that both underlying payment streams were discounted, so this report does not describe it as a net present-value column and does not treat arithmetic reconciliation as proof of discounting. The recognized total in the first column is separate and is stated gross of the sublease-income deduction shown in the middle column.

The MD&A row describes its operating-lease total as net of both sublease income and imputed interest [src-64], which conflicts with Note 7 where imputed interest is shown on a separate row to reach the net-column final row. The MD&A total is therefore not presented here as net of imputed interest.

No disclosure of leases not yet commenced was found, so uncommenced amounts versus recognized liabilities with the year cash becomes payable cannot be established; timing is only via the recognized maturity above. Lease cash is kept distinct from expense, noncash additions and liabilities.

sections.title: Investment and commitments

blocks.text: At December 31, 2025 Palantir held {fact:cash-dec2025} of cash and cash equivalents and {fact:marketable-dec2025} of marketable securities, together {fact:liquidity-dec2025} of cash plus marketable securities [src-68] [src-69]. That stock covered {fact:current-liab-dec2025} of total current liabilities at the same date [src-70]. Total assets were {fact:total-assets-dec2025} against {fact:total-liab-dec2025} of total liabilities, leaving {fact:total-equity-dec2025} of total equity [src-66] [src-67] [src-71]. These are period-end stocks, not annual flows, and marketable securities are not the same as cash available for immediate use.

The company had no outstanding debt balances under the revolving facility as of December 31, 2025 [src-79]. The secured revolving facility provides aggregate commitments of {fact:revolver-capacity-dec2025} with a maturity date of March 31, 2027 [src-78]. Any leverage claim should therefore state whether it subtracts debt alone or also includes lease and commitment obligations, which are disclosed separately.

Future enforceable demands limit how far that period-end liquidity stretches, but they fall due over time rather than all at once. Recognized total lease liabilities were {fact:lease-liab-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-60], a gross carrying amount distinct from the net-column amount after sublease-income and imputed-interest deductions detailed in Investment. Separately, the remaining enforceable noncancelable purchase commitments as of the same date are spread across future payment periods and are set out with their full schedule and definitions in Investment; only enforceable and legally binding contracts are included and obligations under contracts that can be cancelled without a significant penalty are not included [src-62]. One amended cloud-services agreement separately carries a lifetime floor of at least {fact:cloud-commit-fy2025} over ten contract years through September 30, 2033, with {fact:cloud-satisfied-fy2025} of {fact:cloud-current-year-fy2025} for the contract year beginning October 1, 2025 and ending September 30, 2026 [src-57] [src-61]; that lifetime floor is a different scope from the remaining aggregate and neither replaces it nor reconciles with it by subtraction. Paid cash investment of {fact:capex-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-32] and these future commitments use different bases and dates and must not be added together; future commitments are not cash already paid. See Investment for the full payment schedules and what can and cannot be compared.

Palantir paid no cash dividends in FY2025. The filing states the company has never declared or paid any cash dividends on its capital stock [src-77], and that no dividends had been declared as of December 31, 2025 [src-84]. Cash returned to shareholders in FY2025 was therefore only through repurchases, not a dividend.

Cash paid for repurchases was {fact:repurchases-fy2025} in FY2025 as reported on the cash flow statement [src-73]. The matching equity-statement row records retirement of {fact:repurchase-shares-fy2025} (statement amounts in thousands) [src-75] under the program authorized in August 2023 for up to {fact:repurchase-auth-2023} of Class A repurchases [src-76]. The program was terminated in January 2026 [src-80]. The authorization amount is a board limit, not a promise of future spending, and termination means no further purchases under that program should be assumed.

Buybacks did not reduce the share count because new issuance more than offset retirements. Shares outstanding rose to {fact:shares-out-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 from {fact:shares-out-dec2024} a year earlier, growth of {fact:shares-out-growth-fy2025} [src-74]. Stock-based compensation expense was {fact:sbc-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-33]. Looking only at dollars spent on buybacks would overstate the increase in each shareholder's ownership; the per-share result must be read as profit growth less dilution.

Remaining performance obligations were {fact:rpo-dec2025} at December 31, 2025, of which the company expects to recognize {fact:rpo-next12m-pct} as revenue over the next 12 months, {fact:rpo-13to36m-pct} over the subsequent 13 to 36 months, and the remainder thereafter [src-09]. RPO represents only noncancelable contracted revenue not yet recognized, including deferred revenue and in certain instances amounts to be invoiced [src-15]. Cancelable contracted revenue, including customer deposits, is not a remaining performance obligation [src-16], so RPO is a contracted floor rather than a forecast of total revenue.

A broader, option-inclusive signal, total remaining deal value, was larger than RPO at year-end [src-11]. It presumes exercise of all available customer options and no termination of contracts, yet many contracts are subject to termination provisions, including for convenience, with no guarantee against termination or that options will be exercised [src-10]. Government deal value excludes awarded IDIQ contracts where funding has not been determined or guaranteed [src-17]. RPO and contract liabilities are distinct measures that overlap: contract liabilities consist of deferred revenue and customer deposits [src-08], while RPO includes deferred revenue and in certain instances amounts to be invoiced but excludes cancelable contracted revenue including customer deposits [src-15] [src-16]. Neither RPO, deal value nor contract liabilities alone establishes future revenue.

sections.lede: Noncancelable backlog plus option-inclusive deal value, with limits.
sections.title: Demand and remaining performance obligations

blocks.text: A small set of large accounts carries outsized weight among 954 customers at December 31, 2025 [src-03] [src-04]. The filing states {quote:src-83} [src-12]. The mechanism is concentration, not weak performance: if a large relationship is impaired or terminated, or if a large customer reduces spend or does not renew or expand, revenue could decline and results could be adversely affected, with more impact than the loss of a smaller account. The filing presents this as a possibility that could harm results, not as a realized loss.

Contracted backlog may not convert to revenue because conversion depends on options being exercised and contracts not being terminated. Remaining performance obligations were {fact:rpo-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-09]; what that noncancelable measure [src-15] and the broader total remaining deal value measure include is explained in Demand. Cancelable contracted revenue including customer deposits is excluded from RPO [src-16]. The broader measure exceeded RPO at year-end [src-11], but it presumes exercise of all customer options and no termination, yet many contracts are subject to termination provisions including for convenience, with no guarantee against termination or that options will be exercised [src-10]. Awards where funding is undetermined are left out of the government deal-value count, including indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contracts [src-17]. If customers terminate, do not exercise options, or funding does not materialize, contracted amounts would not become revenue, so backlog should be read as conditional rather than assured future revenue.

Government work adds procurement and funding conditions beyond general cancellability. Government revenue was {fact:gov-revenue-fy2025} in FY2025 and U.S. revenue was {fact:us-revenue-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-19] [src-23]. Many government and commercial contracts are subject to termination for convenience, with no guarantee against termination or that options will be exercised [src-10]. Funding that is undetermined is excluded from the government deal-value count, including indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity (IDIQ) contracts [src-17]. A shift in priorities, funding delays or non-exercise of options could therefore leave government backlog unconverted even while reported revenue grew in FY2025.

sections.title: Risk factors

blocks.text: A valuation starts from dated filing inputs, not from operating strength alone. In FY2025 revenue was {fact:revenue-fy2025} and income from operations was {fact:op-income-fy2025} [src-18] [src-27]. Basic earnings per share were {fact:eps-basic-fy2025} and diluted earnings per share were {fact:eps-diluted-fy2025} in FY2025 on basic shares of {fact:shares-basic-fy2025} and diluted shares of {fact:shares-diluted-fy2025} [src-34] [src-35] [src-36] [src-37]. Cash plus marketable securities were {fact:liquidity-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 against {fact:current-liab-dec2025} of current liabilities at the same date, with no outstanding balances under the {fact:revolver-capacity-dec2025} revolving facility maturing March 31, 2027 [src-68] [src-69] [src-70] [src-79]. Shares outstanding were {fact:shares-out-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 [src-74].

The 10-K does not disclose a current share price, a forecast of future revenue or cash flow, a discount rate or a fair value. Cheap or expensive therefore cannot be concluded from the filing alone. Any price analysis must supply its own price assumption, share-count assumption, growth assumption and multiple or discount rate, and test how the conclusion changes when those assumptions change. Future dilution from equity awards and the end of the repurchase program after its January 2026 termination [src-80] are part of that share-count judgment.

Does the dated backlog convert on schedule? Remaining performance obligations were {fact:rpo-dec2025} at December 31, 2025, with {fact:rpo-next12m-pct} expected over the next 12 months, {fact:rpo-13to36m-pct} over months 13 to 36, and the remainder thereafter [src-09]. In the next report, compare recognized revenue against that profile; on-schedule recognition would confirm conversion, while a shortfall or lengthening would weaken it. Do not treat cancelable amounts, including customer deposits, or option-inclusive deal value as assured revenue [src-15] [src-16] [src-10].

Will commitment satisfaction keep pace with hosting demand? Investment explains the amended cloud agreement's lifetime floor and current-year scope. As of December 31, 2025, the Company had satisfied {fact:cloud-satisfied-fy2025} of {fact:cloud-current-year-fy2025} for the contract year beginning October 1, 2025 and ending September 30, 2026, under a commitment to spend at least {fact:cloud-commit-fy2025} over ten contract years through September 30, 2033 — a lifetime floor, not a remaining amount at December 31, 2025 [src-57] [src-61]. In the next report, compare updated satisfaction for that contract year ending September 30, 2026 with third-party cloud hosting in cost of revenue; satisfaction advancing alongside hosting cost would show burn keeping pace, while trailing satisfaction alongside rising hosting cost would enlarge the commitment overhang [src-42]. Keep this contract-year measure distinct from the separate as-of remaining enforceable purchase total, which covers only contracts that are enforceable and legally binding and excludes obligations under contracts that can be cancelled without a significant penalty [src-62]. Satisfied is the source term for progress under the agreement, not physical capacity used.

Does cash conversion persist after working-capital drag? Operating cash flow was {fact:ocf-fy2025} in FY2025 against net income of {fact:net-income-fy2025} in FY2025, when growth in accounts receivable exceeded the contract-liability source as the largest working-capital offsets [src-31] [src-28] [src-50] [src-53]. Next, watch accounts receivable, contract liabilities and the scoped remainder of {fact:cash-remainder-fy2025} in FY2025 after paid purchases of {fact:capex-fy2025} in FY2025; a narrower receivables use or sustained contract-liability growth would support conversion, while renewed widening would weaken it [src-32].

Will issuance again outweigh repurchases without a new authorization? Cash paid for repurchases was {fact:repurchases-fy2025} in FY2025 for {fact:repurchase-shares-fy2025} shares retired, yet shares outstanding still rose {fact:shares-out-growth-fy2025} to {fact:shares-out-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 alongside stock-based compensation of {fact:sbc-fy2025} in FY2025 [src-73] [src-75] [src-74] [src-33]. Because the prior program was terminated in January 2026, the next report should show whether any newly authorized return policy replaces it; without one, further issuance would leave dilution unoffset rather than imply continued purchases under the old program [src-80].

Will the valuation allowance continue to suppress the effective rate? The provision was {fact:tax-provision-fy2025} in FY2025 on pre-tax income of {fact:pretax-fy2025} in FY2025 for an effective rate of {fact:effective-tax-rate-fy2025}, with a full valuation allowance of {fact:valuation-allow-dec2025} at December 31, 2025 maintained [src-29] [src-30] [src-38] [src-45]. If the allowance is released in a future period, comparability would change in that period without adding cash generated then; if it is maintained, the low rate persists on the same conditional basis.

blocks.text: **10-K.** An annual SEC filing covering the business, risks, financial statements and notes.
**FY · Fiscal year.** The company's accounting year. Its closing date can differ from December 31.
**Operating margin.** Operating income divided by revenue. A margin change in percentage points differs from the percentage growth in operating income.
**Segment margin.** The specified segment profitability measure divided by that segment's revenue. Identify the numerator and allocation basis because issuers use different measures.

**Segment contribution.** A company-defined measure of segment profitability whose included costs and exclusions can differ across issuers. Use the report's segment definition before comparing amounts. It is different from a segment's contribution to whole-company growth.
**EPS · Earnings per share.** Net income for each share using the period's weighted-average share count. Diluted EPS also considers potentially dilutive shares, not just year-end shares.
**P/E · Price-to-earnings ratio.** Share price divided by EPS. A scenario's assumed future P/E is not a forecast or the filing's reported share price.
**Operating cash flow · CFO.** Net cash from operating activities, after noncash and operating-balance adjustments. Net income and cash received are different measures.

**Operating cash flow less purchases of property and equipment.** Here, operating cash flow minus cash purchases of property and equipment. It is not a standardized GAAP measure; a broader purchase deduction is labeled separately.
**Depreciation and amortization.** Expenses that allocate asset costs over their useful lives. They are not the same as cash spent buying assets during the current year.
**Current ratio.** Current assets divided by current liabilities. It describes reported short-term coverage, not a guarantee that every asset can immediately be converted into cash.
**Net cash and obligations.** Net cash depends on which cash, investments and debt are included. The report states each definition. Do not add overlapping lease balances and payment schedules.
**Present value.** Future payments discounted to a stated date. Undiscounted payment totals and a reported lease liability need not be equal.
**RPO · Remaining performance obligations.** Contracted goods or services still to be delivered and recognized as revenue. It is not cash already received or a forecast of total revenue next year.
**O&M · Operations and maintenance.** Ongoing operations and maintenance services. The Business chapter explains their role in the company's products, support and revenue recognition.

**IDIQ · Indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity.** A contracting arrangement with delivery and quantity determined through the applicable ordering process. An award or ceiling alone does not establish funded orders or recognized revenue.

The factual source for this report is Palantir Technologies Inc.'s Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025, the period ended 2025-12-31. Reported figures and quotations are distinguished from calculations and analyst interpretations. Calculated ratios and changes use identified filing inputs; they are not presented as separately reported company figures. Registered passages and literal source tables preserve the governing dates, units and notes for the claims they support. The report uses no market data, earnings release, guidance or other outside factual source. A statement that information is not disclosed is scoped to this filing and does not imply zero or erase other disclosed information.

sources.label: Platforms
sources.quote: We have built four principal software platforms: Gotham, Foundry, Apollo, and AIP. Our software platforms provide the critical infrastructure needed to integrate our customers’ data and operations and run their software in virtually any environment.

sources.label: Platform roles
sources.quote: Despite their differences, Gotham and Foundry both serve as central operating systems for our customers. While they vary in specific functionality, they align in approach. AIP provides an integrated architecture to Gotham and Foundry that can bring AI to every decision.

sources.label: Customer count
sources.quote: We work with many of the world’s leading government and commercial institutions. As of December 31, 2025, we had 954 customers.

sources.label: Customer definition
sources.quote: We define a customer as an organization from which we have recognized revenue during the trailing twelve-month period. During the period ended December 31, 2025, we had 954 customers, including companies in various commercial sectors and government agencies around the world.

sources.label: Revenue offering
sources.quote: We generate revenue from the sale of subscriptions to access our software platforms in our hosted environment along with ongoing O&M services (“Palantir Cloud”), software subscriptions in our customers’ environments with ongoing O&M services (“On-Premises Software”), and professional services.

sources.label: Cloud recognition
sources.quote: Revenue associated with Palantir Cloud subscriptions is generally recognized over the contract term on a ratable basis, which is consistent with the transfer of control of the Palantir services to the customer.

sources.label: Segment contribution basis
sources.quote: Contribution is segment revenue less the related costs of revenue and sales and marketing expenses, excluding stock-based compensation expense. Contribution margin is contribution divided by revenue.

sources.label: Contract liabilities
sources.quote: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the Company’s contract liabilities were $812.3 million and $566.4 million, respectively.

sources.label: Remaining performance obligations
sources.quote: The Company’s remaining performance obligations were $4.1 billion as of December 31, 2025, of which the Company expects to recognize approximately 38% as revenue over the next 12 months, 36% as revenue over the subsequent 13 to 36 months, and the remainder thereafter.

sources.label: Remaining deal value
sources.quote: Total remaining deal value presumes the exercise of all contract options available to our customers and no termination of contracts. However, many of our contracts are subject to termination provisions, including for convenience, and there can be no guarantee that contracts are not terminated or that contract options will be exercised.

sources.label: Deal value scale
sources.quote: As of December 31, 2025, the total remaining deal value, as defined in Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Overview—Total Remaining Deal Value, was $11.2 billion.

sources.label: Top customer concentration
sources.quote: Our top three customers together accounted for 16% and 17% of our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

sources.label: On-premises recognition
sources.quote: Revenue is generally recognized over the contract term on a ratable basis.

sources.label: Contribution allocation
sources.quote: To calculate the contribution by segment, we allocate cost of revenue and sales and marketing expenses, excluding stock-based compensation, to an account pro rata based on headcount and time spent on the account during the period.

sources.label: RPO noncancelable only
sources.quote: Revenue allocated to remaining performance obligations represents noncancelable contracted revenue that has not yet been recognized, which includes deferred revenue and, in certain instances, amounts that will be invoiced.

sources.label: Cancelable excluded from RPO
sources.quote: Cancelable contracted revenue, which includes customer deposits, is not considered a remaining performance obligation.

sources.label: IDIQ excluded
sources.quote: When calculating the total remaining deal value of government contracts, we do not include government contracts known as IDIQ contracts, totaling $12.3 billion, as of December 31, 2025, that we have also been awarded, but where the funding of such contracts has not yet been determined
